extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, USPTO enforcement staff, and practitioners subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order approving a Proposed Settlement Agreement resolving a USPTO disciplinary proceeding against a registered patent attorney for unauthorized practice of law and failure to obey court orders, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions. The page documents the standards, regulatory authorities, mitigating conduct, and sanctions procedures applicable to such disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction and authority to approve settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over the matter and the authority to approve the Proposed Settlement Agreement pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly relies on these statutory and regulatory authorities as the basis for approving the parties' Proposed Settlement of Disciplinary Matter submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant, a registered patent attorney is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration before the USPTO subjects practitioners to the Code of Professional Responsibility and attendant disciplinary provisions; the Final Order cites these as the governing standards for evaluating conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law (grounds for discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing to the public and providing legal services in a jurisdiction where not admitted constitutes unauthorized practice of law (example: operating a Virginia law office, listing practice areas and failing to disclose lack of Virginia bar admission, website identifying practitioner as licensed in Virginia, and representing parties before Virginia state courts and the Virginia State Corporation Commission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The North Carolina State Bar's public reprimand for unauthorized practice was used as a stipulated fact supporting USPTO discipline. Anti-patterns include failing to disclose limitations on state practice or affirmatively misrepresenting state licensure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to obey court orders / abandonment of duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally blocking electronic court communications (thereby preventing service of orders), failing to produce ordered documents, and failing to file objections as ordered can constitute abandonment of an attorney's obligations and be prejudicial to the administration of justice (cited violation of Rule 8A(d) of the Rules of Professional Conduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific misconduct here included intentionally blocking emails from the court's communication site, not producing tax returns ordered by the court, and not filing required objections—conduct the state court found prejudicial to justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) and (b)(6) violations as disciplinary predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct such as being publicly reprimanded by a state bar for unauthorized practice and being prohibited from appearing in state courts for misconduct are violations acknowledged to breach 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(5) and 10.23(b)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Respondent expressly acknowledged that the stipulated facts violated these cited regulatory provisions; the Final Order relies on those sections as the legal conclusions supporting discipline (the page cites the section numbers but not their full text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement procedure requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement of Disciplinary Matter under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and, if it satisfies the regulatory requirements, resolves the disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states that the Proposed Settlement Agreement satisfies the requirements of § 11.26 and therefore resolves the disciplinary action initiated by the USPTO based on the stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available and ordered sanctions for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions that may be imposed or agreed to include public reprimand; publication of the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette; notices to state disciplinary agencies and courts; and other discipline as permitted under 37 C.F.R. (e.g., further sanctions under §§ 11.34–11.57).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Respondent was publicly reprimanded; the OED Director was ordered to publish the Final Order electronically and in the Official Gazette; the Order preserves the Office's ability to seek additional discipline for misconduct not addressed in the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of public discipline per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires dissemination of the reprimand and reasons to relevant state agencies and courts; publication locations are specifically named (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior discipline and use of record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order provides that nothing prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by or on behalf of the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves use of the settled record for future enforcement and sentencing considerations; it functions as a warning that settlement does not immunize against future discipline based on the same or similar misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost allocation was agreed as part of the settlement; other settlements might provide for different cost or monetary terms depending on negotiation and regulatory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating remedial measures creditable in discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedial steps—such as correcting misinformation about licensure, notifying clients of non-admission in a state, and withdrawing as counsel in matters where unauthorized—are noted as creditable remedial measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The North Carolina State Bar expressly found these remedial actions taken by the respondent and described them as mitigating; such measures may influence the severity of discipline under the USPTO's evaluative framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of state court prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A prohibition from appearance before a state's trial and appellate courts for a fixed period (nine months in this case) may be limited to court appearances and not otherwise restrict all legal practice in that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes the Superior Court's prohibition did not otherwise limit the respondent's authority to practice law in the state, illustrating nuance in measuring the practical effect of state disciplinary sanctions.
